tools.description:
Adds Search assets (sitelinks, callouts, a structured snippet, a price asset,
business name, business logo and images) to one or more campaigns.

Assets are created once and linked to every listed campaign, in one atomic
request. An asset whose text (sitelink text, callout text, snippet header,
price type, business name) is already linked to a campaign is skipped for
that campaign, so the tool can be re-run safely.

Upload the logo and images first with upload_logo and upload_image and
pass their asset IDs; the logo must be square (1:1), images landscape
(1.91:1) or square.

business_logo_asset_id.description: ID of a square image asset to use as the business logo.

business_name.description: The advertiser name shown with the ad, max 25 characters.

campaign_ids.description: Campaigns to add the assets to.

image_asset_ids.description: IDs of image assets to show with the ad.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

anyOf.description: A price asset: 3-8 offerings of one type.

price.description: Price in the currency of the price asset.

items.description: A sitelink: an extra link under the ad.

description2.description: Second description line, max 35 characters. Give both lines or neither.

sitelinks.description: Sitelinks (Google shows up to 4-6; add at least 2).

anyOf.description: A structured snippet: a header and a list of values.

header.description: One of Google's headers, e.g. Styles, Types, Brands.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: assets_add_campaign_assets
tools.title: Assets Add Campaign Assets

tools.description:
Adds an asset group to an existing Performance Max campaign.

An asset group is a set of creatives (text, images, logos, videos) plus a
final URL and optional audience signals, which Google combines into ads.
Upload images with upload_image / upload_logo first and pass their asset IDs.

audience_ids.description: IDs of audiences to use as audience signals.

campaign_id.description: The ID of a Performance Max campaign.

landscape_logo_asset_ids.description: IDs of landscape (4:1) logo image assets.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

logo_asset_ids.description: IDs of square (1:1) logo image assets.

name.description: The asset group name. Must be unique within the campaign.

search_themes.description: Search themes to use as signals, e.g. "budget tracking app".

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

video_asset_ids.description: IDs of YouTube video assets (see create_youtube_video_assets).

tools.name: assets_create_asset_group
tools.title: Assets Create Asset Group

tools.description:
Creates text assets, e.g. headlines and descriptions, and returns their IDs.

Creating a text asset that already exists returns the existing asset.
Campaign and asset group creation tools accept text directly, so this is
only needed to build reusable assets.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

texts.description: The texts to create assets for.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

tools.name: assets_create_text_assets
tools.title: Assets Create Text Assets

tools.description:
Creates video assets from YouTube videos, for Performance Max asset groups and App campaigns.

The videos must be public or unlisted on YouTube.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

youtube_video_ids.description:
YouTube video IDs, e.g. "dQw4w9WgXcQ" (the `v=` part of a
YouTube URL). Full YouTube URLs are also accepted.

tools.name: assets_create_youtube_video_assets
tools.title: Assets Create Youtube Video Assets

tools.description:
Returns a Performance Max asset group: its status, ad strength, final URLs, linked assets
grouped by field type (e.g. HEADLINE, MARKETING_IMAGE), and audience signals.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: assets_get_asset_group
tools.title: Assets Get Asset Group

tools.description:
Lists the account's image, text and YouTube video assets, newest first.

Check for existing assets before uploading new ones. Images include their
dimensions and the image field types they fit.

asset_types.description: Asset types to include. Defaults to all three.

limit.description: The maximum number of assets to return.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: assets_list_assets
tools.title: Assets List Assets

tools.description:
Unlinks assets (sitelinks, callouts, snippets, prices...) from a campaign. The assets
themselves are kept, and add_campaign_assets can link them again.

Identify links by asset_ids in campaign_id, optionally only those of
field_type (by default every field type the asset is linked as), and/or
by campaign_asset resource names
(customers/<customer id>/campaignAssets/<campaign id>~<asset id>~<field type>).
Find them with the search tool: resource campaign_asset, fields
campaign_asset.resource_name, campaign_asset.field_type, asset.id and
asset.name. If any link is not found, nothing changes.

asset_ids.description: IDs of the assets to unlink from campaign_id.

field_type.description: Only unlink asset_ids linked as this field type.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: assets_remove_campaign_assets
tools.title: Assets Remove Campaign Assets

tools.description:
Uploads an image as an image asset, for use in Performance Max asset groups and App campaigns.

Provide exactly one image source. Images must be at most 5120 KB, and in
JPEG, PNG or GIF format.

The result reports the image dimensions and which image field types the
image fits (by aspect ratio and minimum size):
  - MARKETING_IMAGE: landscape 1.91:1, min 600x314 (1200x628 recommended)
  - SQUARE_MARKETING_IMAGE: 1:1, min 300x300 (1200x1200 recommended)
  - PORTRAIT_MARKETING_IMAGE: 4:5, min 480x600 (960x1200 recommended)
Use upload_logo for logos.

file_path.description:
A path to an image on the machine running the server. Not
available when the server runs as a web service.

image_base64.description: The image content, base64 encoded (a data: URL is also accepted).

image_url.description: A public http(s) URL to download the image from.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

name.description: Optional unique name for the asset. Defaults to the file name.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

tools.name: assets_upload_image
tools.title: Assets Upload Image

tools.description:
Uploads a logo image as an image asset.

Logos must be square (1:1, min 128x128, 1200x1200 recommended) for the
LOGO field, or 4:1 (min 512x128, 1200x300 recommended) for LANDSCAPE_LOGO.
Provide exactly one image source. The result includes a warning if the
image does not fit either logo format.

file_path.description:
A path to an image on the machine running the server. Not
available when the server runs as a web service.

image_base64.description: The logo content, base64 encoded (a data: URL is also accepted).

image_url.description: A public http(s) URL to download the logo from.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

name.description: Optional unique name for the asset. Defaults to the file name.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

tools.name: assets_upload_logo
tools.title: Assets Upload Logo

tools.description:
Creates an App campaign to promote a mobile app (Android or iOS), with its budget,
targeting, ad group and app ad, in a single atomic request. The campaign is created PAUSED.

App campaigns serve across Google Play, Search, YouTube, Discover and the
Display Network, and optimize towards installs or in-app actions.

app_id.description:
The app's store ID: the package name for Google Play
(e.g. "com.example.app"), or the numeric App Store ID for iOS
(e.g. "123456789").

contains_eu_political_advertising.description: Whether the campaign contains EU political advertising.

conversion_action_ids.description: In-app conversion actions to optimize for.

daily_budget.description: Average daily budget in the account currency.

geo_target_ids.description:
Location IDs to target (see find_geo_targets). If empty,
all countries are targeted.

goal.description: What to optimize for, see above.

image_asset_ids.description: Optional IDs of image assets (up to 20).

language_ids.description: Language IDs to target, e.g. 1000 for English.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

name.description: The campaign name. Must be unique in the account.

start_date.description: Optional start date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

target_cpa.description: Optional target cost per install or in-app action.

target_roas.description:
Optional target return on ad spend as a ratio (3.5 = 350%),
for IN_APP_VALUE.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

video_asset_ids.description: Optional IDs of YouTube video assets (up to 20).

tools.name: campaigns_create_app_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Create App Campaign

tools.description:
Creates a Performance Max campaign with its budget, targeting and first asset group, in a
single atomic request. The campaign is created PAUSED.

Performance Max serves across Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail and
Maps, and is suited to website conversion goals. It requires conversion
tracking (see the conversions tools). For app installs use create_app_campaign.

Upload images first with upload_image and upload_logo, and pass the returned
asset IDs. Asset requirements:
  - 3-15 headlines (max 30 characters each)
  - 1-5 long headlines (max 90 characters each)
  - 2-5 descriptions (max 90 characters, at least one of max 60)
  - business_name, max 25 characters
  - 1+ landscape (1.91:1), 1+ square (1:1) marketing images and 1+ square logo
  - Videos are optional; Google may generate videos if none are provided.

Monetary amounts are in the account currency, e.g. 25.5 means 25.50 USD.

asset_group_name.description: The asset group name. Defaults to "<name> asset group".

audience_ids.description: IDs of audiences to use as audience signals.

brand_guidelines_enabled.description:
If true, the business name and logos are set at
the campaign level and shared by all asset groups.

contains_eu_political_advertising.description: Whether the campaign contains EU political advertising.

daily_budget.description: Average daily budget in the account currency.

geo_target_ids.description:
Location IDs to target (see find_geo_targets). If empty,
all countries are targeted.

landscape_logo_asset_ids.description: IDs of landscape (4:1) logo image assets.

language_ids.description: Language IDs to target, e.g. 1000 for English.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

logo_asset_ids.description: IDs of square (1:1) logo image assets.

name.description: The campaign name. Must be unique in the account.

search_themes.description: Search themes to use as signals, e.g. "budget tracking app".

start_date.description: Optional start date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

target_cpa.description: Optional target cost per conversion, for MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS.

target_roas.description:
Optional target return on ad spend as a ratio (3.5 = 350%),
for MAXIMIZE_CONVERSION_VALUE.

validate_only.description:
If true, validates the request without creating the
campaign. Headlines and descriptions are then validated inline.

video_asset_ids.description: IDs of YouTube video assets (see create_youtube_video_assets).

tools.name: campaigns_create_pmax_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Create Pmax Campaign

tools.description:
Adds a responsive search ad to an existing Search ad group.

Give ad_group_id, or campaign_id for a campaign with exactly one ad group.
Headlines and descriptions are strings, or {"text": ..., "pin": ...} to
pin one to a position (HEADLINE_1-3, DESCRIPTION_1-2). Pin sparingly:
pins limit the combinations Google can test.

Google reviews every new ad. Policy problems are reported with their
policy topics, e.g. DESTINATION_NOT_WORKING; fix the text or URL rather
than retrying. validate_only checks the ad, policy included, without
creating it.

ad_group_id.description: The ad group to add the ad to.

campaign_id.description: A campaign with exactly one ad group, instead of ad_group_id.

anyOf.description: A responsive search ad description, optionally pinned to a position.

pin.description: Always show the description in this position.

anyOf.description: A responsive search ad headline, optionally pinned to a position.

pin.description: Always show the headline in this position.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

path1.description: Optional display URL path, max 15 characters.

path2.description: Optional second display URL path, max 15 characters; needs path1.

status.description:
ENABLED serves the ad once approved, if its ad group and
campaign are enabled (it never enables them). PAUSED creates it paused.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

tools.name: campaigns_create_responsive_search_ad
tools.title: Campaigns Create Responsive Search Ad

tools.description:
Creates a Google Search campaign, with a budget, targeting, one ad group, keywords and a
responsive search ad, in a single atomic request. The campaign is created PAUSED.

Use this to drive traffic to a website or web app. For mobile app installs
use create_app_campaign instead.

Look up location IDs with find_geo_targets (e.g. 2840 = United States).
Common language IDs: 1000 English, 1003 Spanish, 1002 French, 1001 German.

Keyword syntax: "[running shoes]" is exact match, '"running shoes"' is
phrase match, and bare text uses keyword_match_type. Negative keywords use
the same syntax, with bare text meaning broad match.

Monetary amounts (daily_budget, target_cpa, max_cpc) are in the account
currency, e.g. 25.5 means 25.50 USD for a USD account.

ad_group_name.description: The ad group name. Defaults to "<name> ad group".

bidding_strategy.description: How to bid. MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS requires conversion tracking.

contains_eu_political_advertising.description: Whether the campaign contains EU political advertising.

daily_budget.description: Average daily budget in the account currency.

final_url.description: The landing page URL for the ad.

geo_target_ids.description: Location IDs to target. If empty, all countries are targeted.

include_search_partners.description: Whether to also show ads on Google search partner sites.

keyword_match_type.description: Match type for keywords without match type syntax.

language_ids.description: Language IDs to target. If empty, all languages are targeted.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

max_cpc.description:
Max cost per click. Required for MANUAL_CPC (the ad group's
default bid); bid ceiling for MAXIMIZE_CLICKS, required there when
the max_cpc_bid guardrail is set. Capped by max_cpc_bid.

name.description: The campaign name. Must be unique in the account.

path1.description: Optional display URL path, max 15 characters.

path2.description: Optional second display URL path, max 15 characters.

start_date.description: Optional start date, YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today.

target_cpa.description: Optional target cost per conversion, for MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS.

target_roas.description:
Optional target return on ad spend as a ratio (3.5 = 350%),
for MAXIMIZE_CONVERSION_VALUE.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

tools.name: campaigns_create_search_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Create Search Campaign

tools.description:
Enables a campaign, so that it starts serving ads and SPENDING its budget.

Before enabling, review the campaign with get_campaign and the account's
current spend with get_spend_overview, and confirm with the user. Refused
if it would break the spend guardrails configured on the server.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_enable_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Enable Campaign

tools.description:
Returns the configuration of a campaign: status, budget, bidding, targeting and, for
Performance Max campaigns, asset groups (or ad groups for other campaign types), plus
performance over the last 30 days.

Monetary values are in the account currency (not micros).

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: campaigns_get_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Get Campaign

tools.description:
Summarizes an account's committed and actual spend, and the spend guardrails in force.

Call this before enabling campaigns or raising budgets. It returns:
  - the total daily budget of enabled campaigns (shared budgets counted once),
  - spend today and this month,
  - account-level spending limits from billing (account budgets), if any,
  - the server's spend guardrails and the headroom left under them.

Google may spend up to 2x a campaign's daily budget on a given day, but
charges at most 30.4x the daily budget per month.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: campaigns_get_spend_overview
tools.title: Campaigns Get Spend Overview

tools.description:
Lists campaigns with their type, status, bidding strategy, daily budget and performance.

Use this to see what is running before creating or changing campaigns.
Monetary values are in the account currency (not micros).

date_range.description: The period for the performance metrics.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

statuses.description: Campaign statuses to include. Defaults to ENABLED and PAUSED.

tools.name: campaigns_list_campaigns
tools.title: Campaigns List Campaigns

tools.description: Pauses a campaign, so that it stops serving ads and spending budget.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_pause_campaign
tools.title: Campaigns Pause Campaign

tools.description:
Pauses or enables ads. Never removes them.

Identify ads by ad_ids within ad_group_id, and/or by ad_group_ad resource
names (customers/<customer id>/adGroupAds/<ad group id>~<ad id>). Find
them with the search tool: resource ad_group_ad, fields
ad_group_ad.resource_name, ad_group_ad.ad.id and ad_group_ad.status. If
any ad is not found, nothing changes. Enabling an ad does not enable its
ad group or campaign.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_set_ad_status
tools.title: Campaigns Set Ad Status

tools.description:
Pauses (or re-enables) auto-applied recommendations for the whole account.

Auto-apply lets Google change campaigns without review: add keywords,
switch to broad match, turn on Display expansion, change bidding
strategies or targets, and rewrite ads. These changes bypass this
server's spend guardrails, so pausing them is recommended for accounts
managed through these tools.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

types.description:
Recommendation types to change, e.g. ["USE_BROAD_MATCH_KEYWORD"].
Defaults to every subscription currently in the other status.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_set_auto_apply_recommendations
tools.title: Campaigns Set Auto Apply Recommendations

tools.description:
Switches a campaign to a standard (non-portfolio) bidding strategy, or changes its target.

The strategy is replaced as a whole: a target that is not given is
cleared, and a campaign using a portfolio strategy leaves it. Budget and
status do not change. A new strategy restarts Smart Bidding's learning
period, so confirm the change with the user first.

  - MANUAL_CPC: you set the bids. default_cpc sets every ad group's
    default max CPC in the same request; otherwise ad groups keep their
    current bids (set_cpc_bids changes them later).
  - MAXIMIZE_CLICKS: cpc_bid_ceiling caps the bid for each click.
  - MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS: needs conversion tracking; optional target_cpa.
  - MAXIMIZE_CONVERSION_VALUE: needs conversion values; optional target_roas.

default_cpc and cpc_bid_ceiling above the max_cpc_bid guardrail are
refused. When that guardrail is set, MAXIMIZE_CLICKS needs a ceiling, and
MANUAL_CPC needs default_cpc if ad groups have default bids above it.

cpc_bid_ceiling.description: Maximum bid per click, for MAXIMIZE_CLICKS.

default_cpc.description: Default max CPC for every ad group, for MANUAL_CPC.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

target_cpa.description: Target cost per conversion, for MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS.

target_roas.description:
Target return on ad spend as a ratio (3.5 = 350%), for
MAXIMIZE_CONVERSION_VALUE.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_set_bidding_strategy
tools.title: Campaigns Set Bidding Strategy

tools.description:
Sets manual CPC bids for a Search campaign's ad group and keywords.

For Manual CPC campaigns with one ad group (as created by
create_search_campaign). Bids are in the account currency. Higher bids
raise cost per click but never the budget; bids above the max_cpc_bid
guardrail are refused.

default_cpc.description:
The ad group's default max CPC, used by keywords without
their own bid.

keyword_bids.description:
Keyword-level max CPC, keyed by keyword in match type
syntax: "[baby name app]" exact, '"baby name app"' phrase, bare text
broad. Use 0 to clear a keyword bid (fall back to default_cpc).

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_set_cpc_bids
tools.title: Campaigns Set Cpc Bids

tools.description:
Renames an ad group, or pauses or enables it. Never removes it.

Enabling an ad group does not enable its campaign. Change its default bid
with set_cpc_bids.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

name.description: A new name, unique within the campaign.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_update_ad_group
tools.title: Campaigns Update Ad Group

tools.description:
Changes the average daily budget of a campaign.

Read the campaign first (get_campaign, or get_spend_overview for the whole
account) and confirm budget increases with the user. Google may spend up
to 2x the daily budget on a given day, but charges at most 30.4x it per month.

If the campaign's budget is shared with other campaigns, the change affects
all of them; this is refused unless allow_shared_budget is true. Spend
guardrails configured on the server (max budget per campaign, max total
daily budget of enabled campaigns, max increase per change) are enforced.

allow_shared_budget.description: Allow changing a budget shared by several campaigns.

daily_budget.description:
The new average daily budget, in the account currency
(e.g. 25.5 means 25.50 USD).

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_update_budget
tools.title: Campaigns Update Budget

tools.description:
Updates campaign settings that are not about budget, bidding or targeting lists.

Only the given settings are changed. None of them can raise a budget or
enable the campaign. Adding networks spreads the same budget over more
placements.

clear_end_date.description: Remove the end date, so the campaign runs indefinitely.

device_bid_adjustments.description:
Percent bid adjustments by device, e.g.
{"DESKTOP": -50, "TABLET": -30, "MOBILE": 0}. -100 stops showing
ads on that device. Range -100 to +100. Manual CPC and enhanced
bidding use them; most Smart Bidding strategies ignore them.

end_date.description: The campaign's last day, YYYY-MM-DD, in the account time zone.

final_url_expansion.description:
OPTED_OUT stops Google from sending clicks to
other pages of the site than the ad's final URL.

location_targeting.description:
PRESENCE shows ads only to people in or regularly
in the targeted locations; PRESENCE_OR_INTEREST (Google's default)
also includes people interested in them.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

name.description: A new campaign name, unique in the account.

target_content_network.description:
Whether a Search campaign's ads also show on
the Display Network (Display expansion).

target_google_search.description: Whether ads show on Google Search.

target_search_network.description:
Whether ads also show on Google search partner
sites (needs target_google_search).

text_asset_automation.description:
OPTED_OUT stops Google from generating
headlines and descriptions from the landing page (Search, PMax).

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: campaigns_update_campaign_settings
tools.title: Campaigns Update Campaign Settings

tools.description: Creates a conversion action, to track a valuable action on a website or web app.

always_use_default_value.description: Always use default_value, ignoring reported values.

category.description: What the conversion represents, e.g. PURCHASE or SIGNUP.

click_through_lookback_window_days.description:
Days after a click (1-90) in which
conversions are attributed to it. Defaults to 30.

conversion_type.description: How conversions are reported, see above.

counting_type.description:
ONE_PER_CLICK (leads, sign-ups) or MANY_PER_CLICK
(purchases). Defaults by category.

currency_code.description:
ISO 4217 currency of default_value, e.g. "USD".
Defaults to the account currency.

default_value.description: The value of a conversion, used when no value is reported.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

name.description: The conversion action name. Must be unique in the account.

primary_for_goal.description: Whether bidding optimizes for this conversion action.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without creating anything.

tools.name: conversions_create_conversion_action
tools.title: Conversions Create Conversion Action

tools.description:
Returns a conversion action's settings, its tag snippets (for website conversions), and
the conversions recorded in the last 30 days, to check that tracking works.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: conversions_get_conversion_action
tools.title: Conversions Get Conversion Action

tools.description:
Lists the account's conversion actions: what counts as a conversion, e.g. purchases,
sign-ups or app installs.

App conversions appear here once their source is linked to the account:
Firebase and Google Analytics 4 (types FIREBASE_* and GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_4_*),
Google Play (GOOGLE_PLAY_*), or third-party app analytics such as AppsFlyer
or Adjust (THIRD_PARTY_APP_ANALYTICS_*). Use their IDs as
conversion_action_ids in create_app_campaign.

include_removed.description: Whether to include removed conversion actions.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: conversions_list_conversion_actions
tools.title: Conversions List Conversion Actions

tools.description:
Chooses which conversion goals a campaign optimizes for and reports as Conversions.

Each goal is a conversion category and origin, written "CATEGORY:ORIGIN",
e.g. "PURCHASE:WEBSITE" or "DOWNLOAD:APP". Listed goals become biddable
for the campaign; every other goal the campaign has is set to not
biddable. This is the campaign-level override of the account-default
goals, useful when one account runs several businesses or apps.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: conversions_set_campaign_conversion_goals
tools.title: Conversions Set Campaign Conversion Goals

tools.description:
Updates a conversion action. Only the given fields are changed.

Set primary_for_goal to choose which conversions bidding optimizes for:
primary actions are used for bidding, secondary ones are only reported.

always_use_default_value.description: Always use default_value, ignoring reported values.

default_value.description: The value of a conversion when no value is reported.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

primary_for_goal.description: Whether bidding optimizes for this conversion action.

status.description: ENABLED, or HIDDEN to stop showing it in the Google Ads UI.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: conversions_update_conversion_action
tools.title: Conversions Update Conversion Action

tools.description:
Uploads offline conversions reported by your backend, attributing them to ad clicks.

Use with UPLOAD_CLICKS conversion actions (see create_conversion_action).
Each conversion needs exactly one click ID: gclid, gbraid or wbraid.
Conversions can be uploaded up to 90 days after the click. Each conversion
is processed independently: the result lists which ones failed and why.

ad_user_data_consent.description:
For users in the EEA, whether they consented to
sending their data to Google for advertising.

items.description: A conversion to attribute to an ad click.

conversion_action_id.description: ID of an UPLOAD_CLICKS conversion action.

conversion_date_time.description: When the conversion happened, as "yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss+|-hh:mm", e.g. "2026-09-27 14:05:00-07:00".

gbraid.description: Click ID for app conversions from iOS web-to-app clicks.

gclid.description: The Google click ID from the landing page URL.

order_id.description: A unique ID for the conversion, used to deduplicate uploads.

wbraid.description: Click ID for web conversions from iOS app-to-web clicks.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without uploading anything.

Returns ids of customers directly accessible by the user authenticating the call.

Use this tool first to discover available customer IDs if the user hasn't

tools.description:
Lists the Google Ads accounts the user can access, with their name, currency, time zone
and whether they are manager (MCC) accounts.

Client accounts directly under an accessible manager account are included
too. To work with such a client account, pass the returned
`login_customer_id` along with its `customer_id` to other tools.

include_client_accounts.description: Whether to include client accounts of manager accounts.

tools.name: customers_list_accounts
tools.title: Customers List Accounts

tools.description:
Updates account-level click tracking: the final URL suffix, tracking template
and auto-tagging. Only the given fields change.

The final URL suffix is appended to every ad's landing page URL and
commonly carries UTM parameters with ValueTrack placeholders, e.g.
"utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign={campaignid}". Pass an
empty string to clear a field. Auto-tagging adds the gclid used for
conversion tracking and offline conversion uploads.

auto_tagging_enabled.description: Whether to add the gclid to ad clicks.

final_url_suffix.description: Query string appended to landing page URLs, without "?".

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.title: Customers Update Account Tracking

tools.description:
Retrieves the selectable, filterable, and sortable fields for a specific Google Ads resource,
including compatible metrics and segments.

Use this tool to find out which fields you can select, filter by, or sort by
when querying a specific resource (e.g., 'campaign', 'ad_group').
This tool also returns metrics and segments that can be selected with the resource.
Their names start with 'metrics.' and 'segments.' respectively.

Do not guess fields, you MUST use this tool to discover them before constructing a query for the
`search` tool.

The responses of this tool should be cached, as they don't change frequently.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

resource_name.description: The name of the Google Ads resource (e.g., 'campaign', 'ad_group').

tools.name: metadata_get_resource_metadata
tools.title: Metadata Get Resource Metadata

tools.description:
Fetches data from the Google Ads API using the search method

    Args:
        customer_id: The id of the customer
        fields: The fields to fetch
        resource: The resource to return fields from
        conditions: List of conditions to filter the data, combined using AND clauses
        orderings: How the data is ordered
        limit: The maximum number of rows to return
        login_customer_id: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

    

### Hints
    Language Grammar can be found at https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/query/grammar
    All resources and descriptions are found at https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/fields/latest/overview
    If the query fails, a ToolError will be raised with the error details.

    For Conversion issues try looking in offline_conversion_upload_conversion_action_summary

### Hint for customer_id
    should be a string of numbers without punctuation
    if presented in the form 123-456-7890 remove the hyphens and use 1234567890

### Hints for Dates
    All dates should be in the form YYYY-MM-DD and must include the dashes (-)
    Date ranges must be finite and must include a start and end date

### Hints for limits
    Requests to resource change_event must specify a LIMIT of less than or equal to 10000

### Hints for conversions questions
    https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/conversions/upload-summaries 


### Hints for all resources
    To find out which specific fields (including compatible metrics and segments) you can select, filter by, or sort by for a given resource, you MUST use the `get_resource_metadata` tool.
    Do not guess the fields. Use the tool to look them up.
    Once you have the fields, ensure the whole field name is used (e.g., 'campaign.id', not just 'id'). Wildcards and partial fields are not allowed.

tools.name: search_search
tools.title: Search Search

tools.description:
Adds keywords to an existing Search ad group, skipping keywords it already has.

Give ad_group_id, or campaign_id for a campaign with exactly one ad group.
Keyword syntax: "[running shoes]" is exact match, '"running shoes"' is
phrase match, and bare text uses match_type. A keyword with the same text
and match type as an existing one (enabled or paused) is skipped and
reported; set_keyword_status re-enables paused ones. New keywords are
enabled, so in an enabled campaign they can start spending right away.

ad_group_id.description: The ad group to add the keywords to.

campaign_id.description: A campaign with exactly one ad group, instead of ad_group_id.

keyword_bids.description:
Optional max CPC per keyword, keyed as in keywords, for
Manual CPC campaigns. Capped by the max_cpc_bid guardrail. Other
keywords use the ad group's default bid.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

match_type.description: Match type of keywords written without [ ] or quotes.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: targeting_add_keywords
tools.title: Targeting Add Keywords

tools.description:
Finds location (geo target) IDs by name, for use in location targeting.

Examples of IDs: 2840 United States, 2826 United Kingdom, 1023191 New York City.

country_code.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code to restrict results, e.g. "US".

locale.description: Language of the returned names, e.g. "en".

location_names.description: Names of places to look up, e.g. ["California", "Toronto"].

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: targeting_find_geo_targets
tools.title: Targeting Find Geo Targets

tools.description:
Lists the account's audiences, whose IDs can be used as Performance Max audience signals.

Audiences are created in the Google Ads UI (Tools > Audience manager) and
combine your data segments (e.g. app users, site visitors), interests and
demographics.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

tools.name: targeting_list_audiences
tools.title: Targeting List Audiences

tools.description:
Sets the audience signals of a Performance Max asset group.

Signals are hints that help Google find converting users faster; they do
not restrict who sees the ads. Two kinds are supported:
  - audiences: reusable Audience resources (combinations of your data,
    interests and demographics). Find their IDs by querying the `audience`
    resource with the search tool.
  - search themes: phrases describing what your customers search for,
    e.g. "habit tracker app".

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

mode.description:
add, remove or replace. With replace, signals of both kinds that
are not listed are removed.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: targeting_set_audience_signals
tools.title: Targeting Set Audience Signals

tools.description:
Sets the locations a campaign targets or excludes.

Find location IDs with find_geo_targets. mode "add" adds the given locations,
"remove" removes them, and "replace" makes the campaign's location targeting
exactly the given targeted and excluded locations. Removing all targeted
locations is refused, since the campaign would then target all countries.

location_ids.description: Location IDs to target, e.g. [2840] for the United States.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: targeting_set_geo_targets
tools.title: Targeting Set Geo Targets

tools.description:
Pauses or enables ad group keywords. Never removes them.

Select keywords by text in match type syntax ("[running shoes]" exact,
'"running shoes"' phrase, bare text broad) within ad_group_id or
campaign_id (all its ad groups), and/or by criterion ID. Criterion IDs
are only unique within an ad group: give ad_group_id or campaign_id with
them, or write them as "<ad group id>~<criterion id>". Find IDs with the
search tool (resource ad_group_criterion). If any keyword is not found,
nothing changes. Enabling a keyword does not enable its ad group or
campaign.

ad_group_id.description: Only change keywords of this ad group.

campaign_id.description: Only change keywords of this campaign.

criterion_ids.description:
Keyword criterion IDs, "<ad group id>~<criterion id>"
pairs, or ad_group_criterion resource names.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: targeting_set_keyword_status
tools.title: Targeting Set Keyword Status

tools.description:
Sets the languages a campaign targets.

Common language IDs: 1000 English, 1003 Spanish, 1002 French, 1001 German,
1005 Japanese, 1017 Chinese (simplified). A campaign without language
targeting targets all languages.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.name: targeting_set_language_targets
tools.title: Targeting Set Language Targets

tools.description:
Sets campaign-level negative keywords, which stop ads from showing for matching searches.

Works for Search and Performance Max campaigns. Keyword syntax: "[free app]"
is exact match, '"free app"' is phrase match, and bare text is broad match.
With mode "replace", negative keywords not in the list are removed.

login_customer_id.description: Optional manager customer ID to use as the login-customer-id header.

validate_only.description: If true, validates the request without changing anything.

tools.title: Targeting Set Negative Keywords
